title: Grove: Servo Dial
intro: Turn a Grove knob and a servo follows it, like a remote-controlled dial.

steps.title: Read the knob
steps.text:
The Rotary Angle Sensor is in port **A0**, an **analog** port. `analogRead` gives a number from 0 to `ANALOG_MAX` (1023 on an Uno), depending on how far the knob is turned.

**Your task:** run it, open the Serial Monitor and turn the knob all the way each way.
hints: Drag the knob in the simulator.
One end gives 0, the other gives the biggest number.
Turn it slowly and watch the numbers change smoothly.

checks.label: Turned the other way: a big number
The number changes when I turn the knob

steps.success: The knob gives your program a number it can use.

steps.title: The servo follows
steps.text:
A servo turns from 0 to 180 degrees. `map()` changes the knob's number (0 to `ANALOG_MAX`) into an angle (0 to 180).

**Your task:** fill in the blank with the biggest angle.
hints: The servo's biggest angle is in the text above.
The line is `int angle = map(knob, 0, ANALOG_MAX, 0, 180);`
steps.success: Turn the knob and the servo copies it.

outro: You turned a Grove knob's number into an angle with **map()** and moved a **servo** with it.
stretch: Make the servo only use 45° to 135°.
Print the angle on the Serial Monitor too.
Make the servo move the opposite way to the knob.
